suite.description: State-machine and durable-operation fixtures of multi-device identity (IDENTITY-PROFILE-01 §12.3; LFCP-WIRE-01 §107).

conventions.steps: inputs.steps are performed in order; expected.steps gives each step's outcome and the facts it asserts.
conventions.references: A step case `wire:<id>` names a case of LFCP-IDENTITY-TEST-VECTORS-01, `profile:<id>` one of IDENTITY-PROFILE-TEST-VECTORS-01; the step outcome equals that case's expected outcome. `bytes_of` names a case whose exact bytes a step sends in another context, with the outcome the step states.
conventions.client_outcomes: Outcomes without a case are client-procedure results (phase states of IDENTITY-PROFILE-01 §9.2, statuses of §6); they have no wire code.

cases.description: Register DEV_A, write, revoke it, accept an old-head unit, close the epoch, quarantine the unit beyond the frontier and rebuild

rule.text: Revocation without rotation leaves old-head units acceptable until the closing KEY_EPOCH; beyond its frontier they are STALE_DATA_EPOCH and replicas rebuild without them.

steps.action: replicas R1 and R2 accept the registration
DEV_A writes sequence 1 at I1
DEV_B self-registers and writes; BRIDGE writes at I8
BRIDGE writes at I8
OWNER revokes DEV_A
R1 receives DEV_A sequence 2 at the old head I1, latest I9, and merges it
OWNER closes epoch 0
R2 receives the same unit after K1
R1 learns K1 and rebuilds without DEV_A sequence 2

assertions: R1, which merged the unit before the revocation closed the epoch, and R2, which saw it only after, end with the same accepted set (LFCP-WIRE-01 §19.1).

cases.description: Revoking DEV_A suspends DEV_B by the cascade; re-certification by the root makes it active again; DEV_B units at each head

rule.text: A suspended device is not revoked; the root or a managing device may re-certify it with a chain that avoids the revoked issuer.

steps.action: DEV_B self-registers with [CERT_B, CERT_A]
DEV_B writes at I2
OWNER revokes DEV_A
DEV_B writes at I9
DEV_B cannot re-certify itself
OWNER re-certifies DEV_B with [CERT_B2]
DEV_B writes at I10

assertions: The unit at I9 stays refused after I10: activity is evaluated at the head a unit references.

cases.description: Self-registration proposed on a stale head, re-evaluated on the new head; the same DEVICE_GRANT proposed twice

rule.text: A proposer that meets CONTROL_HEAD_MISMATCH synchronises and classifies its phase on the accepted chain; a repeated record is not a transition and the intent is complete.

steps.action: DEV_B proposes its self-registration on J2 while the coordinator head is I1
DEV_B synchronises, classifies the register phase as pending and proposes a fresh record on I1
A second installation of the same intent finds devices[DEV_B].leaf_id = id(CERT_B)
Had it proposed a fresh DEVICE_GRANT with the same leaf, rule 5 refuses it (shown for DEV_A)
The exact bytes of a committed record sent again

assertions: No record is proposed twice as a new transition; a re-sent exact record gets the same ACK.

cases.description: The owner revokes BOB's grant: every device of BOB is inactive; a re-grant restores them without new device records

rule.text: Revoking the root's standing silences all its devices; restoring it restores them without re-registration.

steps.action: OWNER revokes J1
DEV_C writes at I11
DEV_C opens X at I11
OWNER grants BOB again
DEV_C writes at I12

assertions: Activity returns with standing; no DEVICE_GRANT is needed.

cases.description: Reconciliation of X against I's Control state: revocations first, then registrations, then keys; idempotent

rule.text: Revocations first; registrations of personal devices active in I and not registered in X; keys by the ledger; a second run proposes nothing.

steps.action: I's state at P4: DEV_A and DEV_B registered, (OWNER, PAIR_J) consumed
X's state: DEV_B self-registered with [CERT_B, CERT_A], DEV_A bound only as an intermediate
Step 1: I's revocation of (OWNER, PAIR_J) is proposed on X with reason 0
Step 2: DEV_A (intermediate-only in X) is registered with I's chain; DEV_B has the same leaf certificate ID and needs nothing
Step 3: every epoch of X the reconciler holds is sealed to DEV_A and DEV_B unless the ledger records it
A service device whose issuer I has revoked is never registered in X: the revocation reaches X first and X refuses the chain (as chain_through_revoked_issuer)
The Identity Resource as its own target: steps 1 and 2 are vacuous, step 3 seals I's epochs to DEV_B
A second run
Two reconcilers race: the loser meets CONTROL_HEAD_MISMATCH, synchronises and classifies its phases as complete

assertions: Registration and key delivery are reconciled independently; an equal leaf certificate ID says nothing about packages.

cases.description: Two managing devices revoke DEV_A concurrently with different reasons: one record; the other phase is complete

rule.text: Revoked with any other reason, by anyone: complete; the operation continues with the rotation test.

steps.action: OWNER revokes DEV_A with reason 1
DEV_A2 (also managing) had proposed DEVICE_REVOKE {OWNER, DEV_A, 2} on I8: CONTROL_HEAD_MISMATCH
After synchronising, a fresh revocation would be refused
DEV_A2 classifies its revoke phase
DEV_A2 continues with the rotation test of §8.1

assertions: A different reason recorded by another installation is complete, not superseded.

cases.description: An invitation accepted by a device of DAVE: the claim names the root, the device registers itself and keys its root

rule.text: The claimant is the root; the device self-registers, seals the DEKs it holds to its root and adds the Resource to the roster.

steps.action: OWNER invites INVITE
DEV_D, a device of DAVE, claims with claimant DAVE, signed by INVITE
DEV_D registers itself
DEV_D seals epoch 0 to DAVE
DAVE opens X and reads
DEV_D adds X to the roster of I

assertions: A device claimant would be refused (claim_by_bound_claimant); the root is the member.

cases.description: Pairing a personal device DEV_B through PAIR_J in I: phases 1 and 2, keys, request, limits, reuse and retries

rule.text: A pairing session yields at most one approved payload; nothing is signed for D_B before the consume is committed (N9).

steps.action: DEV_A creates the pairing device
DEV_A seals every epoch of I to PAIR_J (same root) and makes the root's unit 1 retrievable before showing the link
The link
B verifies the initial change (from a Snapshot only after the root's unit 1)
B writes its request as PAIR_J
A shows the fingerprint
Phase 1: consume with digest(CERT_B)
Phase 2: DEVICE_GRANT with field 2
Keys of I to DEV_B
A consumed PAIR_J receives nothing
B learns the consume through the revoked-reader prefix
A manager that lacks a DEK of I or the root's unit 1 offers no link
40 sessions created and cancelled one after another, then a session completes: cancelled pairing devices free their places
R at 32 live devices: no link until one is revoked
Two managers approve different requests of one session: the loser classifies phase 1 as superseded and signs nothing
A phase-2 record for another digest is refused
Lost ACK of phase 2: the exact bytes are re-sent and answered with the same ACK
Crash between phase 1 and phase 2: resume from the journaled payload; the signed certificate equals the journaled one

assertions: One link used by two installations: sequential reuse writes sequence 2 of PAIR_J; concurrent equivocation excludes both units and A sees no request.
R at 31 live devices: PAIR_J takes the 32nd place, the consume frees it and D_B is registered (W §17.4 rule 8 counts live bindings).

cases.description: Pairing a service device BRIDGE_O: bind-only in I, results learnt from the scoped Resources

rule.text: A service device is bound in I and never registered there; only a certificate whose digest equals the approval proves the result; a timeout is never a decision.

steps.action: Phase 1: consume with digest(CERT_SO)
Phase 2: bind-only DEVICE_GRANT in I
BRIDGE_O cannot write in I
Registration in X, a candidate of the approved scope
Every candidate unreachable after approval
The first verified certificate with digest d arrives from X
A certificate for BRIDGE_O with another digest
A candidate where BRIDGE_O is registered but no leaf with digest d was ever accepted
A crashes after the bind-only DEVICE_GRANT was accepted, before its ACK was persisted; on restart the register phase is

assertions: B restarts and resumes from its persisted candidates; neither path depends on PAIR_J after its revocation.

cases.description: Request validation and the feasibility check before anything is committed

rule.text: A preset whose complete future chain fails W §7.3 steps 1 and 4 and W §17.4 rules 4 to 6 and 8 is not offered.

steps.action: A valid request
A request written by another pairing device into this one
The descriptor changes between display and confirmation
A manager with a chain of three certificates: Full is not offered
A manager whose mask lacks 3 cannot issue Edit
An Edit device cannot issue at all
A service scope trimmed to nothing
The manager's own authority is re-checked after a head change

assertions: No consume is proposed for a preset that fails the check.

cases.description: A revoker whose chain passes through the target re-certifies first

rule.text: The revoker's own chain MUST NOT pass through D; it first obtains a fresh chain from the root.

steps.action: DEV_B (chain [CERT_B, CERT_A]) wants to revoke DEV_A: the pre-check refuses
OWNER re-certifies DEV_B with [CERT_B2]
The revocation then proceeds (shown by the root)
Self-retirement leaves rotation to another installation

assertions: A device cannot re-certify itself (device_grant_self_recertify_suspended).

cases.description: Rotating I while pairing sessions are open

rule.text: The new DEK is sealed to every Principal with holds(P, 1) at the new head, open pairing devices included; consumed or cancelled ones receive nothing.

steps.action: Two open sessions PAIR_J and PAIR_K
A rotation of I seals the new DEK to OWNER, DEV_A, PAIR_J and PAIR_K
One session closed (PAIR_J cancelled): the other continues
A consumed or cancelled pairing device receives nothing
A foreign reader in I and a rotator without 6
A revoker with 7 but not 6 in a Resource with a foreign reader
With both 6 and 7
In I, where every reader is of the root, 7 alone suffices

steps.outcome: rotates and seals to every reader

assertions: The rotator test of §8.1 decides; no assumption that every reader of I is a personal device replaces it.

cases.description: Crash and concurrency at every ACK of pairing approval and of revoke plus rotate

rule.text: Phases are classified against the accepted chain; a KEY_EPOCH is rebuilt, never re-proposed as it was.

steps.action: Crash before the consume ACK; the chain lacks the record
Crash after the consume ACK; the chain holds it with this digest
Crash after the revoke ACK
A concurrent rotation by another writer after the revocation
A reader revoked between planning and sending packages
Partial package delivery
A rotator crashes after the KEY_EPOCH ACK and before any package

assertions: A second rotator may commit the next KEY_EPOCH after a bounded wait; no installation reconstructs a DEK it does not hold.

cases.description: The final frontier comes from the rotator's verified accepted set

rule.text: A server's Have Vector is a fetch hint; a sequence the rotator could not fetch and verify stays outside the frontier.

steps.action: The server advertises DEV_A 1..100; only 1..2 are fetchable and verify
A hole: 1, 2 and 4 verified
An advertised unit that fails authorization (DEV_B at I9)

assertions: The frontier never trusts an advertised range.

rule.text: A revocation that removes no registered reader never triggers a rotation; one rotation covers every exposing revocation since the last.

An unbound tombstone without descendants
An out-of-scope binding revoked
An already suspended device revoked
A never-reading device revoked
An intermediate-only device with a reading descendant revoked
Three exposing revocations in one epoch
A former member cannot issue the tombstone at all

assertions: Exposure is computed from the Resource's own chain alone.

rule.text: Access refused alone, or revocation proven through the Control read for a revoked reader; uploads are checked by object.
